feedback: Your Task 7 answer is very strong, with complete segment decoding, the empty signature, RFC 7519 Section 6.1, CVE context, and the correct algorithm allow-list fix. Task 6 is also solid because it identifies the four hash families, compares likely alternatives, and ranks MD5 and SHA-256 as the highest rotation priorities. Task 3 loses credit because Artefact C decodes to the wrong plaintext, and the submitted Artefact B string appears malformed even though the expected message is stated. Task 10 answers the board themes but drifts into broad governance language and does not cite the exact AES key and IV evidence as cleanly as needed. The capstone recovers AES, ROT13, JWT basics, and the layered memo, but D2 omits Artefact 04 entirely, D1 has only a partial failure map, and D3 needs clearer cost-aware controls mapped to at least two findings each.
